name: Bauernstoss
description: Bauernstoss is a regional variant of Schafkopf played almost exclusively in the Palatinate (Pfalz) region of Germany. Unlike the Bavarian national game, Bauernstoss simplifies the trump structure significantly: the four Jacks are always the highest trumps, followed by the permanent trump suit (usually Hearts or Diamonds depending on the village), and there are no variable 'Solo' or 'Wenz' games. It is a pure partnership point-trick game played with high velocity and heavy 'klopfen' (knocking) to double the stakes.

history.origins: Originates from the village of Erfweiler and surrounding areas in Southwest Germany. It represents an older, more 'rustic' branch of the Schafkopf family tree that did not evolve into Skat.
timeline: 19th Century: German point-trick games diverge into Schafkopf (Bavaria) and Skat (Altenburg).
1920s: Bauernstoss solidifies as the local tavern game of the Palatinate forest region.
Present: Kept alive by local clubs and village tournaments, distinct from the standardized German Schafkopf Association rules.
history.cultural: A game deeply rooted in local identity. Players often use specific Palatine dialect terms for the cards (e.g., 'De Alt' for the Old One/Highest Trump).
history.evolution: The name 'Bauernstoss' (Farmer's Push/Kick) likely refers to the aggressive nature of the bidding or the 'pushing' of points to the partner.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite).
setup.deck: 32-card German or French deck. Ranks: A, 10, K, Q(Ober), J(Unter), 9, 8, 7.

rules.objective: Score more than 60 points (out of 120) to win the deal.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Knocking**: Before the first card is played, players can 'Knock' (Klopfen) to double the value of the game. 2. **Play**: Forehand leads. Players must follow suit (Farbzwang). If they cannot follow suit, they must play a trump (Stechzwang). If they have no trumps, they can play any card. 3. **The Trick**: Highest trump wins. If no trump, highest card of led suit wins. 4. **Scoring**: Winner of the trick takes the cards. Points are counted at the end.
keyRules: Jacks belong to the trump suit, not their printed suit.
Stechzwang (Must Trump) applies: unlike Bavarian Schafkopf where you can discard on a void, here you MUST trump if able.
Partners must cooperate without verbal signals.

strategy.basic: Lead your aces early (the 'Volle') to secure 11 points before they get trumped. Since you must trump if void, long suits are dangerous for opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Management: With 4 Jacks and 7 Heart trumps (11 total), the trump distribution is key. If you have J♣ and J♠, you control the game. Draw out opponents' trumps before playing your 10s.
strategy.advanced: The 'Schmieren' (Smearing): If your partner is winning a trick, throw your 10 or Ace on it. This adds 10 or 11 points to your pile instantly. Knowing when to smear vs when to hold an Ace for a later trick is the mark of an expert.
tips: Count the trumps played. Once the Jacks are gone, the Ace of Hearts is the boss.
If you are weak, lead a singleton to force opponents to play high or trump.

variations.name: Alter Schoofkopp
variations.description: A variant from Niederhochstadt where the Queens are also trumps (below Jacks), making a very long trump suit.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Differences such as adding queens to the trump suit are described textually and will be wired into engine overrides later.

variations.name: Ramsch
variations.description: Played if everyone passes (in bidding variants). Object is to lose points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Ramsch scoring and objective changes are documented in prose; structured engine overrides are planned for a future revision.

scoring.description: Strokes (Striche) on a slate or coin payments.
scoring.winCondition: Usually played for a set duration or until the slate is wiped.

synthesis.shortDescription: The rustic cousin of Schafkopf from the Palatinate forest. With fixed partnerships and the four Jacks permanently leading the charge, Bauernstoss is a game of pure point-capture efficiency. Knock on the table to double the stakes and trust your partner to smear the Aces.
